 What's happening now
 • Nationwide ground stop: JetBlue has called off the remainder of its domestic flights for the evening and more major airlines may be preparing to do the same , a source tells CNN, after federal officials halted all US flight departures due to safety concerns from a telecommunications outage . The issue stems from a problem with network routers that cascaded nationwide, an airline source said.
 • Travel nightmare: An estimated 1.5 million people were stranded by flight cancellations, according to analysis by the data firm Cirium. The skies are emptying as flights that were already in the air come in for landing.
 • No timetable for resolution: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin warned that there’s no known time frame for resolving the issue and that he expects an extended process.
 • No known threat: Mullin said the ground stop did not stem from a threat to the US and was not linked to this week’s disruptive Microsoft outage. Preliminary reports indicate this was not a cyberattack , law enforcement sources told CNN.

 US-bound flights from Asia also suffer delays and cancellations
 By June Jeong 
 US-bound flights from major airports across the Asia Pacific have also been affected by the nationwide ground stop.
 Overnight flights from Incheon International Airport in the South Korean capital Seoul to Detroit, Guam, Atlanta and San Francisco face delays of up to two hours.
 A Delta Air Lines flight from Hong Kong to Los Angeles was canceled, and another to the city was delayed.
 A flight from Shanghai to Detroit and another from Singapore to San Francisco also faced delays.

 JetBlue and Air Canada call off remainder of US flights for Friday
 By Alexandra Skores 
 JetBlue Airways and Air Canada are calling off their remaining US flights for Friday, the airlines said in their own statements.
 “Due to the nationwide FAA mandated ground stop, JetBlue is canceling all remaining flights this evening with the exception of Europe-bound departures from JFK and Boston,” JetBlue said. “Flights already in the air are continuing to their destinations.”
 JetBlue said it expects disruptions to continue into tomorrow, with additional cancelations.
 Air Canada said it would cancel all of its flights between Canada and the US for the rest of the evening.
 “Flights between Canada, the Caribbean and South America that pass through U.S. airspace could also be affected,” Air Canada said in a statement.

 Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport has run out of space to park planes
 By Pete Muntean 
 Airplanes are parked on the tarmac on Friday, at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport in Arlington, Virginia. 
 Jonathan Ernst/Reuters 
 Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport does not have any more space to park planes, an airport source said.
 The FAA has issued an alert that the airport can no longer accept diversions, the source added.
 Some context: With so many aircraft unable to fly because of the nationwide groundstop, airports are running out of gates and tarmac space to park planes.

 Here’s why US authorities have — so far — concluded aviation incident was not an attack
 By Josh Campbell 
 A “whole of government” response to Friday’s incident involving national air traffic by multiple law enforcement and intelligence agencies has still not identified a nefarious attack, a senior US security source told CNN.
 Authorities continue to believe the issue was caused by a communication software issue rather than an intentional act, the source said, even as cyber specialists coast to coast are still investigating the incident.
 US law enforcement and intelligence agencies began receiving internal updates from aviation officials notifying them something was amiss right around when television screens inside agencies’ 24-hour command centers in the agencies’ headquarters began alerting officials to the issue Friday.
 It prompted officials at the FBI, Department of Homeland Security, and even the US National Security Agency — which leads efforts to counter foreign cyber threats — to spring into action.
 “Still no indication this was an attack,” the senior security source said late Friday. The source added the collective security response included “drilling down on” the various means the US government’s aviation system connects to networks that could potentially be exposed to bad actors.
 The source said efforts by US security services to identify any potential “node of attack” are expected to continue “at full speed” in the coming days, as cyber threats can sometimes eventually be located deep inside computer networks.
 Compounding the problem are antiquated aviation networks spread across the country that need to be investigated, the source added.
 “The (US) aviation networks and servers are old and spread across a wide swath of territory and won’t be totally cleared until we get boots on the ground to give a close look at the networks impacted,” the source said.

 Just under 10,000 flights delayed today, tracking platform reports
 By Tori B. Powell 
 Flights continue to be canceled and delayed amid the nationwide ground stop.
 According to the aviation tracking platform FlightAware, there have been 9,814 total delays and 5,117 total cancellations within, into or out of the US today as of 8 p.m. ET.
 The Federal Aviation Administration issued the ground stop today at approximately 4 p.m. ET. The delays and cancellations reported by FlightAware account for the entire day and not just following the ground stop announcement.

 This traveler found out — too late — about the ground stop
 By Julia Vargas Jones 
 Like countless others this evening, Adanma Uzor has no idea when when she can return home. She was already in an Uber en route to Chicago’s O’Hare International Airport when she read the United Airlines text alert warning her about delays and the possible cancellation of flights.
 “We are sorry to let you know” about the nationwide ground stop, the 4:43 p.m. CT message began. She was set to return home to New York after a work trip.
 The message had arrived minutes before she left for the airport, but she hadn’t checked her phone until the Uber was already on the highway, she told CNN.
 Uzor tried her luck anyway. “I figured I’d still go, cause you never know,” she said.
 On arrival, she was told to scan her boarding pass on a kiosk, to see options of vouchers for a hotel and meals.

 Over 5,000 flights canceled, number expected to grow, data shows
 By Emma Tucker 
 A person looks at a departures board showing cancelled flights at Chicago O'Hare International Airport, on Friday. 
 Jim Vondruska/Reuters 
 More than 5,000 flights have been canceled across the US, and the number is expected to grow, as the nationwide ground stop remains in effect with no end in sight, according to FlightAware and Cirium.
 There were 26,284 flights scheduled to depart from the US today, and over 15% of them were cancelled or didn’t take off, according to Cirium, an aviation analytics company.
 At least 827 flights were diverted today, with 670 returning to their departure airports and the rest rerouted to other airports, according to Cirium data.
 Most of those flights were rerouted to Chicago O’Hare, Charlotte, Denver, Dallas-Fort Worth and Houston, according to Cirium.
 The flights categorized as “no fly” in the data did not depart within 180 minutes of the scheduled departure time, Cirium said.
 “We anticipate that number will grow today,” the company said.

 More than 700 flights in the US canceled for Saturday

 More than 700 flights within, into, or out of the United States are canceled for Saturday, according to flight data tracker FlightAware.
 As of 7:45 p.m. ET, Delta Air Lines canceled 5% of its flights, United Airlines canceled 4% of its flights and American Airlines canceled 2% of its flights.
 Airlines also often make preemptive decisions about flight cancellations for many reasons, including weather, maintenance issues or crew scheduling.

 "Very old and antiquated" tech may be to blame, former transportation secretary says
 By Dalia Faheid 
 “Very old and antiquated” technology that air traffic controllers use to guide planes in and out of airports may have contributed to the nationwide meltdown today, former Secretary of Transportation Ray LaHood told CNN affiliate WEEK.
 “I assume that there’s been some serious glitch with that technology,” he told WEEK from Peoria International Airport in Illinois.
 Specifically, LaHood said there was likely an issue at an FAA facility.
 LaHood called the ground stop “a national calamity.”
 “Thousands of people are relying on getting on an airplane and it’s kind of incomprehensible to think that this could happen in the 21st century.”

 Frustrated passengers wait in long lines at JFK airport
 By Zachary Slater 
 Passengers who deplaned after their flights were canceled, wait in lines stretching hundreds of people long at baggage claim in JFK’s Terminal 4. 
 Zachary Slater/CNN 
 After deplaning from canceled flights, frustrated passengers are waiting in lines hundreds of people long at baggage claim in Terminal 4 at John F. Kennedy International Airport.
 The lines snake all the way to Delta’s baggage help desk, where just a few workers are helping stranded passengers.
 Anyone wanting to get their checked bags back tonight is in for a long wait.

 Published Nov 13, 2026, 7:24 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 FAA nationwide ground stop throws many of Saturday's sports games into question
 By Jacob Lev 
 With the FAA ordering a nationwide ground stop, sports in all leagues and competitions could be impacted on Saturday.
 According to ESPN’s Pete Thamel , many college football teams are having flight issues, including No. 6 Texas, No. 8 Tennessee and No. 19 Ole Miss.
 The SEC said it is “aware” of the ground stop and remains “in close communication with our member institutions to assess potential disruptions and coordinate appropriate responses.”
 Many other teams in the Big 12 and Big Ten are also have reported issues.
 “Due to the national FAA ground stop impacting team travel, the Big 12 Conference is evaluating potential changes to Saturday’s football schedule,” the conference said in a statement to CNN. “The Conference will continue to monitor the travel disruptions alongside its member institutions and provide updates for Saturday’s games.”
 CNN has reached out to the Big Ten for comment but did not immediately hear back.
 There are also five National Basketball Association (NBA) games and 14 National Hockey League (NHL) games scheduled for Saturday.
 CNN has reached out to the NBA and NHL for comment.
 The NFL told CNN that all teams are scheduled to travel on Saturday and the Detroit Lions and New England Patriots are already in Munich, Germany ahead of their international game at the Allianz Arena on Sunday.

 Published Nov 13, 2026, 7:23 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 Faced with no other options, travelers at Miami airport find out they can’t fly
 By Carolina Peguero and Emma Tucker 
 People wait in a check-in line at the British Airways counter in Miami International Airport after the FAA announced a nationwide ground stop on Friday, in Miami, Florida. 
 Joe Raedle/Getty Images 
 There was still a sense of calm among travelers arriving at Miami International Airport as they began to navigate the ramifications of a nationwide ground stop on all departures.
 People have been learning of the news after trying to check in for their flights. Some are walking up and down hallways trying to figure out their next steps. Others have already been waiting at the airport for a few hours, realizing they have no other options to get to their destinations.
 At the American Airlines information desks, workers are helping passengers understand what options they might have. Travelers holding their suitcases who had connecting flights, hoping to head on to international destinations, have eventually realized their plans wouldn’t pan out how they expected.
 One traveler named Chelsea, who was with her children, told CNN she was planning to surprise them with their destination point. She found out about the advisory as her husband was returning their rental car.
 Their flight went from delayed to canceled.
 “No rental cars, no hotels with shuttles. … Just trying to find a solution at this point,” Chelsea said.
 The family is “very disappointed,” she told CNN, adding that her children didn’t know where they were headed but found out from announcements at the airport that their flights had been impacted.

 Planes are parked on the tarmac at Dallas Fort Worth International Airport in DFW Airport, Texas, Friday after the Federal Aviation Administration grounded all flights nationwide.

 Major airlines could shut down operations for the rest of tonight as the FAA outage continues, an airline source said.
 “Stay tuned for the big airlines to shut down for the evening,” the source said.

 It’s been just over three hours since federal officials issued a rare nationwide order to halt all departing flights in the US. Here’s how the ground stop affected air travel throughout the country:

 Published Nov 13, 2026, 7:11 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 Flights within Alaska and Hawaii can still depart, airlines say
 By Tori B. Powell 
 The nationwide ground stop currently in effect won’t affect the country’s noncontiguous states, according to Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines.
 The airlines said that flights within Alaska, nearby neighboring islands, and Hawaii, as well as flights from the West Coast to Hawaii and international flights from Honolulu, can still depart.
 “Because of the significance of the ground stop, we have canceled some flights and diverted others,” Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines said in a statement. “When the ground stop is lifted, it will take time for our operations to get back on track for the rest of the day.”
 Pacific-bound flights have been cleared to depart from San Francisco International Airport, the airport said in a post on social media today.
 Read more 
 Published Nov 13, 2026, 6:45 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 Traveler opts for 6-hour drive to Montreal instead of waiting out ground stop in Newark
 By Brian Stelter 
 Yehya Siddiqui, 37, saw the news of the ground stop while waiting at Newark airport for a flight home to Montreal.
 His first thought? “Everybody’s going to be renting cars,” he said. Siddiqui, who was visiting New York for client meetings, booked a rental SUV immediately, and now he’s planning to drive across the border to Canada. 
First, though, he said he’ll stop in Albany, New York to sleep for the night.
Siddiqui was originally supposed to fly home on Thursday, but thunderstorms scuttled that flight, and he was rebooked for Friday.
 “I don’t know how long the FAA will shut this down,” he said, so he’s opting to drive the six and a half hours home instead.
 At Newark airport, a long line of people walked toward the rental car counters around 6:30 p.m. ET, hoping cars would still be available.
